  • Funding: €1,000 per month, plus a one-time €1,000 travel grant

Guidelines & Files

Timeline

Aug 1, 2026 at 12:00 PM: Call opens

Sep 30, 2026 at 12:00 PM: Final application deadline

Oct 31, 2026 at 12:00 PM: Results announced

Visegrad–Taiwan Scholarships offer funding for PhD candidates (early-stage researchers), and doctoral and postdoctoral scholars (experienced researchers) to study/conduct research in Taiwan. The program is run in cooperation with the National Science and Technology Council (NSTC), Taiwan.

Eligible candidates: Visegrad–Taiwan Scholarships offer funding for PhD candidates (early-stage researchers), and doctoral and postdoctoral scholars (experienced researchers) to study/conduct research in Taiwan.

Areas of support: Quantum Technology, AI and Robotics, IT, Cyber Security, Social Sciences and Humanities, or other.

Length of support from 1 to 10 months.

The amount of the support is €1,000/month for each scholar + €1,000 in the form of a one-time travel grant (tuition and other costs associated with the research are covered by the Taiwanese side).

Prospective applicants from Taiwan can contact Chief of Cabinet Jiří Sýkora for further references.

If other universities in Taiwan (not included in the list of host universities) are also interested in hosting scholars from V4 countries through this program, the respective Taiwanese host professor should first contact NSTC to express their intention and obtain the host approval from their home university in order to be listed in the table.

NSTC Contact:
Dept. of International Cooperation and Science Education NTSC; Viven Li, Researcher
e-mail: vvlee@nstc.gov.tw
tel.: 02-2737-7150

The application must be submitted on-line via My Visegrad between August 1 and September 30, 12.00 PM CET (noon) and must include the following enclosures in English or accompanied by certified translation:

  • A scan of the highest obtained university diploma with transcript (in English or translated into English);
  • Scanned verified confirmation of current enrollment/involvement in PhD study/research issued by the present university/institution (document on a letterhead paper and confirmed—i.e., stamped and signed—by the present university/institution;
  • A scanned letter of acceptance or an equivalent document (e.g., invitation letter) from the host university/institution containing a detailed working plan of the study/research period (not older than 3 months when submitting the application)—please consult the list of eligible host institutions (above);
  • Scans of two letters of recommendation, with one of them issued by the supervisor (leader of the research group in case of postdoctoral scholars) at the present university/institution, stating that the supervisor/leader agrees with the proposed stay abroad.

item.title: Film / Talks Purple Rain (1984) 27 Sep 2026 / 16:00
item.description:
The film follows The Kid, a talented young man who uses music to escape his abusive situation at home. A member of the band The Revolution, The Kid is the star of the most famous and disputed club in Minneapolis.

When he meets singer Apollonia, The Kid fights not to repeat his father’s abusive patterns, while struggling to keep together his band, threatened by rival musician Morris Day, who wants to take his place.

Part autobiographical, Purple Rain was made to promote the eponymous album, which propelled Prince to the peak of his career: with 25 million copies sold worldwide, it became one of the best-selling albums of all time.

Don’t Look Back

This event is part of the film cycle “Don’t Look Back”, which includes six documentaries and film-concerts.

item.title: Talks Cultivating the murky with ruderal plants 27 Sep 2026 / 16:00
item.description:
As part of the exhibition Inês Zenha. Murky Waters, the artist talks to researcher Teresa Castro about ruderal plants: species that grow and thrive spontaneously in environments disturbed by human activity.

They are not merely the “weeds” of cities and industrial estates, or the successful colonisers of wastelands and urine-soaked tree pits. Flourishing in the everyday ruins of capitalism, they are exceptional companions for thinking and, above all, for cultivating turbulence.

This conversation will be conducted in Portuguese, with simultaneous interpretation into English. The session will also include interpretation in Portuguese Sign Language.

Speakers

Credits

item.title: Film / Film-Concert / Talks Summer of Soul (2021) 26 Sep 2026 / 16:00
item.description:
The six-week festival took place at Mount Morris Park (today Marcus Garvey Park), in Harlem, New York City, and featured big names such as Stevie Wonder, Nina Simone, Sly and the Family Stone and B.B. King, amongst others.

Commonly known as the Black Woodstock, the Harlem Cultural Festival drew a crowd of 100 thousand people, although this historic achievement had been erased from the collective memory for almost 50 years.

Registered by Hal Tulchin, the nearly 40-hour footage were archived until they were rescued by the director Ahmir Khalib Thompson. The film was officially launched in 2021 at the Sundance Festival and received several awards, including an Oscar.  

Don’t Look Back

This event is part of the film cycle “Don’t Look Back”, which includes six documentaries and film-concerts.

item.title: Concert Tchaikovsky’s Serenade for Strings 24 Sep 2026 / 20:00
item.description:
• Gulbenkian Orchestra

    In 1962, the Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation decided to establish a permanent orchestral ensemble. Originally with only twelve musicians (strings and continuo) it was named “Orquestra de Câmara Gulbenkian”. This collective was successively enlarged and today the “Orquestra Gulbenkian” (the name it has adopted since 1971) has a permanent body of sixty instrumentalists, a number that can be expanded depending on the repertoire.

    This structure allows the Gulbenkian Orchestra to interpret works from the Baroque and Classical periods, a significant part of 19th century orchestral literature and much of the music of the 20th century, including works belonging to the current repertoire of the traditional symphonic orchestras. In each season, the orchestra performs on a regular series of concerts at the Gulbenkian Grand Auditorium in Lisbon, where it has had the opportunity of working together with some of leading names of the world of music (conductors and soloists). It has also performed on numerous locations all over Portugal, in an effort to decentralize music and culture.

    The orchestra has been constantly expanding its activities in the international level, performing in Europe, Asia Africa, and the Americas. In the recording field, Orquestra Gulbenkian is associated to labels as Philips, Deutsche Grammophon, Hyperion, Teldec, Erato, Adès, Nimbus, Lyrinx, Naïve and Pentatone, among others, and this activity was recognized with several international prizes.

    Hannu Lintu is the Music Director of the Gulbenkian Orchestra since 2023.

item.title: Film / Film-Concert / Talks The Last Waltz (1978) 20 Sep 2026 / 17:00
item.description:
Advertised as a farewell concert, the show attracted an audience of 5000 people and brought together several special guests, such as Bob Dylan (who refused to be filmed until the last minute,  ser filmado até ao último minuto, putting the project’s funding at risk), Eric Clapton, Neil Diamond, Emmylou Harris, Joni Mitchell, Van Morrison and Neil Young, among others.

The concert was filmed by director Martin Scorsese, who transformed it in a 116 minute documentary, considered one of the best film-concerts of all time.

The film includes live performances, interrupted by studio sessions and interviews with musicians Rick Danko, Levon Helm, Garth Hudson, Richard Manuel and Robbie Robertson, who reflect on the history of the band and life on tour. 

Don’t Look Back

This event is part of the film cycle “Don’t Look Back”, which includes six documentaries and film-concerts.

item.title: Stop Making Sense (1984) 20 Sep 2026 / 20:00
item.description:
Jonathan Demme follows the band at the height of their career, creating an immersive experience for the audience. The film starts with singer David Byrne alone on the stage, which takes shape gradually as the other elements are brought together.

Filmed during the course of three nights, the documentary includes the band’s first hits, like Psycho Killer, the latest singles at the time, as well as songs from the singer’s solo repertoire and from the Tom Tom Club project, by drummer Chris Frantz and bassist Tina Weymouth.  

Hailed by critics as one of the best concert films ever made, Stop Making Sense is an essential film for Talking Heads fans, offering a glimpse into the New Wave scene of the late 1970s and early 1980s.

Don’t Look Back

This event is part of the film cycle “Don’t Look Back”, which includes six documentaries and film-concerts.

Filmed during Bob Dylan’s famous transitional period to rock and the electrical guitar, this documentary follows the musician from his arrival in England, on April 26th 1965, and the last concert of the tour at the Royal Albert Hall, on May 10th.

The director had access to the backstage, offering a glimpse into Dylan’s public and private life, from concerts to hotel room conversations, recording his tumultuous relationship with singer-songwriter Joan Baez during a critical phase of his musical career.

A number of well-known figures are featured in the film: Dylan’s agents Albert Grossman and Bob Neuwirth, musicians Donovan, Joan Baez, Marianne Faithfull and Alan Price (Animals), and the beat poet, Dylan’s close friend, Allan Ginsberg, among others.

Don’t Look Back

This event is part of the film cycle “Don’t Look Back”, which includes six documentaries and film-concerts.

item.title: Concert / Talks Sammy Baloji. Missa Utica 19 Sep 2026 / 20:00
item.description:
Event Slider

Date

  • 20:00 / Cancelled 20:00 / Sold out Saturday, 20:00

Location

Pricing

10% – Cartão Gulbenkian and Cartão Gulbenkian Mais

Missa Utica by Sammy Baloji is a performance that revisits the early contacts between Europe and the Kingdom of Kongo, intertwining colonial memory, spirituality, and music.

In partnership with Contemporânea, the CAM presents, at the intersection of live performance, concert, and artistic montage, Missa Utica (2024) by Sammy Baloji (DR Congo, 1978). The work brings together performers Fiston Mwanza Mujila, Pytshens Kambilo, and Barbara Drazkow Drążkowska in a dialogue with the historical ties between Europe and the Kingdom of Kongo. Memories of colonisation interweave with spirituality, colonial memory, music, and performance.

Based on extensive research conducted by Sammy Baloji on Congolese objects scattered across European collections, Missa Utica returns to the initial contact between Western Christianity and the Central African region, which occurred around the final years of the 15th century. Episodes linked to the evangelical religious conversion of the Kingdom of Kongo, colonial power dynamics, and the resulting cultural and political transformations are revisited within this context.

The title refers to Utica, an ancient Roman city located within the borders of modern-day Tunisia—a place chosen as a symbol, as it was there that the first African bishop of Black descent, Dom Henrique, son of King Afonso I of Kongo, was consecrated. This historical moment serves as a starting point to reflect on how European Christianity spread across the African continent and the relationships it forged with slavery, colonisation, and processes of cultural erasure.

A key highlight of the work is the Missa Luba, a liturgical composition created in the Belgian Congo in the 1950s by Franciscan missionaries, based on traditional Congolese musical styles. Although it gained visibility in Europe and the United States, little was said about the colonial conditions that allowed for its emergence. In Missa Utica, this past resurfaces, but now intertwined with Congolese rumba, recited verses, and improvised sounds.

Throughout the performance, music, text, and image merge into layers; different temporalities occupy the same space without hierarchy. Bodies speak for themselves, bringing forward histories of displacement, resistance, and survival. Voices emerge as traces of struggle and persistence against erasure. In this way, memory does not remain solely in the past—it reappears.

Rather than committing to a single format, Missa Utica blends elements of modern ritual with traces of sound performance. The work follows Sammy Baloji’s ongoing investigation into how colonial archives shape identities, historical narratives, and collective imaginaries.

Missa Utica is part of the Performance Program My Center is Not in the Solar System, under the artistic direction of Celina Brás and curated by Alexandra Balona.

item.title: Talks Murky Waters 19 Sep 2026 / 18:30
item.description:
Inês Zenha talks to curators João Mourão and Luís Silva about the questions running through Murky Waters: the relationship between body, water and transformation, and the ways artistic practice can imagine spaces of resistance, vulnerability and care.

Starting from the paintings, sculptures and installations on display, the conversation turns to the research and production processes behind them, and to themes such as queer embodiment, the materiality of ceramics and painting, and the tensions between the sacred and the profane, purity and contamination.

More than a reading of the exhibition, this is a reflection on how art can create new images, narratives and experiences for thinking about the body and the structures that shape it.

This conversation will be conducted in Portuguese, with simultaneous interpretation into English. The session will also include interpretation in Portuguese Sign Language.

Speakers

Credits

Main image

Exhibition ‘Murky Waters' in Museo Centro de Arte Dos de Mayo © Sue Ponce, Courtesy Museo CA2M.

The Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation reserves the right to collect and keep records of images, sounds and voice for the diffusion and preservation of the memory of its cultural and artistic activity. For further information, please contact us through the Information Request form.

item.title: Talks A Dreamed Conversation 19 Sep 2026 / 17:00
item.description:
During this conversation, Mathieu Copeland, curator of The Exhibition of a Dream, and FM Einheit, who composed and performed the songs based on the dreams of sixteen artists, will revisit the exhibition’s second incarnation since its premiere in Paris in 2017 and reflect on FM Einheit’s artistic trajectory and body of work.

Conceived as a record, The Exhibition of a Dream comprises sixteen dreams interpreted as songs, performed within otherwise empty galleries and following the temporary, evolving forms of mandalas. Drawing direct inspiration from the dreams of filmmakers, playwrights, poets and writers, these sonic compositions unfold over time, tracing patterns that are both fleeting and deliberately constructed.

FM Einheit was invited to take hold of this body of dreams and set it to music. Following initial demos sketched in his Steinschlag studio in Bavaria, FM Einheit collaborated with musicians Volker Kamp, Robert Poss, Susan Stenger, Erika Stucky, Saskia von Klitzing, and the singers of the Gulbenkian Choir. The dream interpretations were recorded live in 2017, both publicly and privately, in the Gulbenkian Foundation’s two amphitheatres in Lisbon: the Open-Air Amphitheatre and the Grand Auditorium. Underscoring the complex beauty inherent in the genesis of a dream, an experience shared within our inner worlds, the exhibition explores what it means to create mental images in the minds of those experiencing these dreams, opening them to new interpretations.

This conversation will be conducted in English, with simultaneous interpretation into Brazilian Portuguese. The session will also include interpretation in Portuguese Sign Language.

Speakers

The Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation reserves the right to collect and keep records of images, sounds and voice for the diffusion and preservation of the memory of its cultural and artistic activity. For further information, please contact us through the Information Request form.

item.title: Grants Gulbenkian Energy Communities Supporting renewable energy community projects in Portugal that empower citizens to play an active role in the energy transition. closes 16 Sep 2026 Open call
item.description:
Since Portugal introduced its first legal framework for collective self-consumption of renewable energy in 2019, community-led renewable energy initiatives driven by citizens, associations and local authorities have gradually begun to emerge.

Although Renewable Energy Communities (RECs) offer significant environmental, economic and social benefits, fewer than ten are currently operating in Portugal. RECs enable citizens to come together to generate, share, consume and store renewable energy, creating value both for their members and for the communities in which they operate.

In response to the absence of dedicated public funding for citizen-led Renewable Energy Communities, the Gulbenkian Foundation has partnered with Coopérnico – Sustainable Development Cooperative to support civil society organisations working alongside citizens, local authorities and other local stakeholders.

The initiative seeks to address some of the key barriers to establishing Renewable Energy Communities, including the upfront investment required to launch projects, limited technical capacity within local organisations and communities, and low levels of energy literacy among citizens.

Through this call, the Gulbenkian Foundation expects to fund 10 projects, with grants of up to €30,000 each.

Objectives

Grant funding will be awarded to projects that contribute to:

  • expanding decentralised renewable energy generation and local energy use;
  • strengthening the involvement of local authorities, community organisations and cooperatives in community energy initiatives;
  • promoting collective action through participatory governance models;
  • increasing the participation of economically vulnerable citizens and households;
  • encouraging Renewable Energy Communities in rural and low-density areas, while promoting greater territorial diversity;
  • fostering diversity and representation in project leadership and coordination.

Application process

The call for proposals will take place in two stages.

  • In the first stage, between 14 July and 16 September 2026, applicants are invited to submit an Expression of Interest outlining their proposal to establish a Renewable Energy Community, assessed on the basis of the proposed project and the profile of the lead organisation. The 20 highest-ranked applications will progress to the second stage.
  • In the second stage, between 19 and 30 October, the organisations behind the 20 shortlisted proposals will take part in a two-week online capacity-building programme. Following this programme, and based on the development of the proposals, 10 finalist projects will be selected to receive grant funding from the Gulbenkian Foundation.

Webinar

A webinar to present the call and answer questions will take place on 21 July, from 17:30 to 18:30, with prior registration required, including an open Q&A session.

Conditions

  • Grants are available only to legal entities established and registered in Portugal.
  • The amount awarded to each project will be determined during the final selection process and will not exceed €30,000.
  • Eligible costs include: administrative expenses associated with establishing a Renewable Energy Community; licensing procedures; the purchase and installation of renewable energy generation equipment for collective self-consumption and local energy sharing.

Eligibility

Applications are open to locally based, non-profit legal entities registered in Portugal.

This call is intended to support Renewable Energy Communities at an early stage of development. Therefore, at the time of application, organisations must not have a licensing application pending or already approved by the Directorate-General for Energy and Geology in Portugal; or have received funding from any public or private organisation for projects relating to Renewable Energy Communities or collective self-consumption.

How to Apply

  • Only applications submitted online will be accepted;
  • Register at  MyGulbenkian;
  • Before submitting your application form, check all the eligibility criteria and be sure to read the Call Conditions (available in the documents section);
  • Applications may only be submitted once all the mandatory fields of the form have been completed and the documents required under the Call Conditions have been uploaded;
  • Don’t forget to click “submit application”. Try not to submit your application in the last few days leading up to the deadline to avoid any unforeseen last minute problems.

Faq

Who can apply?

This call is open to civil society organisations that represent citizens' interests, are actively engaged with their local communities, and are committed to playing an active role in the energy transition through democratic participation.

Do members of a Renewable Energy Community need to be located within the same parish or municipality?

No. Under Portuguese legislation, members do not need to be located within the same parish or municipality. However, they must be located within 2 km of the renewable energy generation system (or 4 km in low-density areas), or be connected to the same electricity substation.

Can an informal group of citizens apply?

No. The Gulbenkian Foundation provides grants only to legally established non-profit organisations. An informal group of citizens may partner with an eligible organisation whose statutory objectives are aligned with this call, but it cannot receive funding directly from the Foundation.

Can a municipality or parish council apply? What about a local energy agency or another municipal body?

No. This call is intended to support citizen-led Renewable Energy Communities (RECs), meaning communities led by organisations representing groups of citizens, such as associations or cooperatives.

Municipalities, Parish Councils, local energy agencies and other municipal bodies may participate as project partners, but they cannot lead, manage or submit an application.

Is a recently established association, cooperative, foundation or other non-profit organisation eligible?

Yes.

Can an organisation submit more than one application?

No. Each organisation may submit only one application.

Are partnerships required?

No. However, partnerships formally confirmed through Letters of Support submitted with the application may strengthen the quality and feasibility of the proposal.

Are project partners required to make a financial contribution?

No. Partners may contribute in other ways, for example by making rooftops or other suitable spaces available for the installation of photovoltaic panels.

Can a research centre established as a non-profit private legal entity apply?

No. This call is not intended to fund research projects.

Can projects involve partnerships with for-profit organisations?

Yes. Projects may include local businesses or service providers with a relevant role in the community, provided that their participation falls within the scope of their corporate social responsibility activities rather than constituting a commercial service.

These organisations cannot become the sole owners of the project assets. Ownership must be shared.

Will certain territories be given priority?

Yes. Preference will be given to applications from low-density areas or territories facing greater social, economic or environmental vulnerabilities. Applicants should explain and justify these circumstances in their proposal.

Can an organisation that is already receiving funding from the Gulbenkian Foundation apply?

Yes. However, priority will be given to organisations that have never received, or are not currently receiving, funding from the Foundation. Projects that are already being funded by another public or private organisation will not be eligible for support.

Can the grant be used to recruit staff?

No.

What are the requirements for successful applicants?

In addition to managing the grant in accordance with the Foundation's funding rules, successful applicants must participate in all activities organised as part of this initiative, including the capacity-building programme delivered by Coopérnico.

They will also be required to submit a progress report after the start of the project and a final report, using templates provided by the Foundation.

Will there be an information session?

Yes. A free online webinar will take place on 21 July 2026, from 17:30 to 18:30 (Lisbon time). 

Can a national or regional organisation submit a project with a local focus?

Yes, provided that the proposal clearly demonstrates its local relevance.

Can project partners be changed after the application has been approved?

Yes, provided that the change does not compromise the objectives or successful implementation of the project.

Do the future members of the Renewable Energy Community need to be identified in the application?

Applicants should identify the prospective members of the Renewable Energy Community.

Can an organisation with no previous experience in the energy sector apply?

Yes. This call is intended for organisations that consume electricity, not for organisations already operating in the energy sector.

Should the project be selected, the organisation will need to amend its statutes in order to establish a Renewable Energy Community. The costs associated with this process are eligible for funding under the grant.

Can organisations based in the Autonomous Regions of the Azores and Madeira apply?

Yes. Organisations based in the Autonomous Regions are fully eligible to apply.

The only difference concerns the competent licensing authority. In mainland Portugal, the registration, prior control and licensing of Renewable Energy Communities are carried out by the Directorate-General for Energy and Geology (DGEG). In the Autonomous Regions, these responsibilities lie with the Regional Directorate for Energy (DRE) in the Azores and the Regional Directorate for Energy and Climate Change (or Regional Directorate for Energy) in Madeira.

What is meant by "vulnerable citizens or households" for the purposes of this call?

For the purposes of this call, vulnerable citizens or households are those experiencing financial hardship and at risk of energy poverty, as demonstrated by their eligibility for, or receipt of, the Social Electricity Tariff or the Social Natural Gas Tariff.

The aim is to support households for whom energy costs represent a significant financial burden and who stand to benefit most from the cost savings associated with participation in a Renewable Energy Community.

Does an REC have to be based on photovoltaic solar energy?

No. A Renewable Energy Community (REC) may choose other renewable energy generation systems. However, within the scope of this call, only solar photovoltaic generation systems will be considered, as they are currently the most cost-effective technology and the quickest to license and install.

Can a condominium (residential building or multi-family building) apply?

No. A condominium is not eligible because it does not constitute a formally established civil society organization.

Contacts

Questions about this call should be sent to: [email protected].

Before contacting us, please read the Call Conditions carefully and consult the Frequently Asked Questions, as your query may already be answered there.

item.title: Visual and Sound Artist Residency UPCOMING Opens: September 15, 2026
item.description:
Visual and Sound Artist Residencies facilitate mobility and artistic exchanges of V4 citizens in the fields of visual and sound arts, including design, music, video and film, new media and mixed media.

At-a-Glance Criteria

  • Eligibility & Scope: Applicants V4 citizens age 18+; the residency must take place in a V4 country other than the applicant’s country of citizenship/residence.
  • Duration & timing: Lasting 2 months between January 10 and December 31
  • Funding: €6,000 total per project — €3,000 for the resident and €3,000 for the host organization

Guidelines & Files

Timeline

Sep 15, 2026 at 12:00 PM: Call opens

Oct 15, 2026 at 12:00 PM: Final application deadline

Dec 20, 2026 at 12:00 PM: Results announced

Jan 10, 2027 at 12:00 PM: Project start

Visual and Sound Artist Residencies are open to artists working in the following disciplines: Visual Arts (including performance art, textile art and architecture), Design (fashion, costume, jewelry, ceramics and furniture design, visual communication), Music/Sound (interpretation, sound installation, sound performance, composition) and Video/Film/New Media/Mixed Media (including video installation).

  • The residency must be implemented in a V4 country, other than that of the applicant’s citizenship/residence
  • The period of support is 2 months
  • Residencies can take place between January 10 to December 31
  • Reapplying of previously supported artists is possible only for a residency in a V4 country different that of the previous residency project
  • The amount of the support is €3,000 for resident and €3,000 for the host organization for the two months of the residency; each res­i­dency project receives €6,000 in total.

The Final Report in the form of a questionnaire is  to be submitted by the artist and the host institution no later than 30 days after the end of the residency. To ensure the timely disbursement of the final installment, residents are kindly requested to complete the questionnaire within 30 days after the conclusion of their residency. The questionnaire is completed in the My Visegrad system.

Additionally, residents are required to upload images captured during their residency and provide web links to any related posts. 

The host organization is responsible for completing, printing, and signing a separate questionnaire. Following this, residents are kindly requested to upload the completed questionnaire from the host organization (pdf file) as part of their Final Report through My Visegrad system and submit the entire report.

Technical problems with online application and other questions should be addressed to Project Manager Martin Marciňa.

The application form must be submitted via My Visegrad by October 15 at 12.00 PM (noon). The online application system opens at noon on September 15.

Your application must include the following enclosures:

  • Copy of your ID or passport
  • Artistic portfolio  (file or link to artist's website)
  • The applicant chooses the host organization and submits a preliminary confirmation of acceptance

Explore more

Do you have questions?

Check our Frequently Asked Questions for answers about this opportunity.

Get informed on time – Don't miss the next call!

Enter your email to get reminders about upcoming deadlines for Visual and Sound Artist Residency.

item.title: Literary Residency Program UPCOMING Opens: September 15, 2026
item.description:
Literary residencies are intended to develop and promote V4 literature by providing support to the work and mobility of talented writers of fiction and non-fiction, poets, essayists, critics as well as literary translators, publicists and journalists from V4 countries by creating a platform for literary exchanges.

At-a-Glance Criteria

  • Program structure: The program supports Literary Residents hosted by 4 institutions, with residencies held either in Spring or in Autumn Edition.
  • Eligibility & composition: Participants from V4 countries, hosted by an institution, working on individual literary projects while participating in joint literary events.
  • Funding: €1,300 for Spring Edition and €2,600 for Autumn Edition.

Guidelines & Files

Timeline

Sep 15, 2026 at 12:00 PM: Call opens

Oct 15, 2026 at 12:00 PM: Final application deadline

Dec 20, 2026 at 12:00 PM: Results announced

May 1, 2027 at 12:00 PM: Project start

The Visegrad Literary Residency Program, consists of a series of residency stays and literary events addressed to writers of fiction and non-fiction, poets, essayists, critics as well as literary translators, publicists and journalists from the Visegrad Countries (Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland and Slovakia). The Villa Decius Association acts as the Coordinator of the Program.

It is based on a partnership of 4 Host Institutions, one in each V4 country: 

Národní institut pro kulturu (Czech Cultural Institute, previously Arts and Theatre Institute) in Prague

Petőfi Irodalmi Múzeum (Petőfi Literary Museum) in Budapest, 

Stowarzyszenie Willa Decjusza (Villa Decius Association) in Krakow and 

Slovenské literárne centrum (Slovak Literary Centre) in Bratislava.

The Program will provide opportunities to host from and in all V4 member states and support work and mobility of talented Literary Residents, to create a platform for information exchange and to support development and promotion of the V4 literature in Central Europe.

Program will enable 32 Literary Residents to carry their literary projects in 4 Host Institutions in one of the given periods: 1st May – 12th June (Compact Spring Edition) or 1st September – 30th November (Regular Autumn Edition).

item.title: Visual Artist Residency in New York, USA UPCOMING Opens: September 15, 2026
item.description:
Visual Artist Residency in New York provides artists with the chance to be inspired in a variety of spectacular artistic settings of Brooklyn. Every year, four artists get the incredible opportunity to engage with peers and focus on process and experimentation. The program gives artists complete freedom during their residency, but also provides resources and weekly lectures for guidance and feedback.

At-a-Glance Criteria

  • Eligibility: Visual artists from V4 countries, with good spoken and written English.
  • Residency: Lasting 2 months from July 1 until August 31
  • Funding: for each artist €7,000 to cover accommodation, travel, subsistence, and necessary materials.

Guidelines & Files

Timeline

Sep 15, 2026 at 12:00 PM: Call opens

Oct 15, 2026 at 12:00 PM: Final application deadline

Dec 20, 2026 at 12:00 PM: Results announced

Jul 1, 2027 at 12:00 PM: Project start

The residency program at International Studio & Curatorial Program in New York, USA creates an environment for inspiration, dialogue, and experimentation. It allows four artists (one from each Visegrad country) to experience life and work in a unique community where creativity is applied to the everyday and offers conditions that enrich the creativity.

ISCP was founded in 1994 with the mission to support and enhance the professional development of emerging to mid-career artists and curators from around the world, introduce New York audiences to exceptional international art practices and engage the communities of Brooklyn and the New York City area through public programs that enrich the appreciation and understanding of contemporary art.

The program is suited to visual artists, artists with interdisciplinary practices.

  • Applicants are visual artists from V4 countries, only a single artist per V4 country annually
  • Good knowledge of English both spoken and written
  • Applicants have not received art scholarships in New York in the past (preference)
  • The residency period is 2 months, July 1 to August 31
  • The amount of support for each artist is €7,000 to cover accommodation, travel costs, subsistence during the stay, as well as purchasing of materials necessary for the respective artistic activity

For more information about general conditions and selection criteria, read the Rules of the Visegrad Artists Residency Program

Technical problems with online application should be addressed to Project Manager Martin Marciňa.

The application form must be submitted via My Visegrad by October 15 at 12.00 PM (noon). The online application system opens on September 15.

Your application must include the following enclosures:

  • Copy of your ID or passport
  • Your CV and motivation letter (including your project plan)
  • Artistic portfolio (file or link to artist´s website)

Applicants are selected on the basis of their previous work, their potential contribution to the residency stay in New York, as well as the potential benefit they can draw from the program. Only one artist per V4 country is supported annually.

Explore more

item.title: Fashion Residency in Milan, Italy UPCOMING Opens: September 15, 2026
item.description:
Fashion Residency Program in Milan (IT) opens unique opportunities for professionals and researchers from the Visegrad countries from the field of fashion, design and related areas. An experience based in Milan, the heart of the fashion industry, for two months with the possibility of visits to Rome as well. Research and "live fashion" within the context of individual exploration supported by lectures and experiences with Accademia Costume & Moda.

At-a-Glance Criteria

  • Eligibility: Applicants V4 citizens, age 18+, good written/spoken English (Italian is a plus).
  • Applicants may come from fashion or non-fashion backgrounds and showing a clear interest in the Italian fashion supply chain.
  • Selection criteria: A creative approach demonstrated by previous work/projects plus residency plan, and a defined research proposal.
  • Timing: lasting June 1 – July 31 in Milan, Italy
  • Funding: €6,000 per artist to cover living expenses.

Guidelines & Files

Timeline

Sep 15, 2026 at 12:00 PM: Call opens

Oct 15, 2026 at 12:00 PM: Final application deadline

Dec 20, 2026 at 12:00 PM: Results announced

Jun 1, 2027 at 9:00 AM: Project start

Accademia Costume & Moda (ACM) has a long tradition in educating professionals in  the areas of Fashion, Costume for the Performing Arts, Communication and Management.

Founded in 1964 in Rome by Rosana Pistolese, costume and fashion historian, as well as costume designer for theater, television and cinema, and also fashion and costume writer and publicist.

Thanks to the great talent and passion of its founder, Accademia has become over time a laboratory of ideas and research. An Italian prestigious private academy and cultural association that offers unique resources to carry out varied research within the wider scope of the fashion industry.

During the Fashion Residency in Milan, four selected professionals, with a background or an interest in the broad field of fashion, access to a campus studio designed for creative work, research and networking. Participant will receive individual as well as group guidance with lectures and discussions regarding topics such as Contemporary Art, Fashion History, Sociology, Understanding Contemporary Fashion, Portfolio Building and Communication, as well as others.

Fashion Residents will get series of lectures about art & fashion, fashion & society, fashion fabrics history, knitwear history and industry overview, and special masterclass about fashion design & production ethics too. They will also take part in planned visits to museums and cultural institutions as well as possible trade fairs. To enhance the research and educational support, access to Luigi Bocconi Library is granted and a special excursion to the seat of AMC in Rome is included too.

During the residency the main emphasis is on research projects. However, there is also a program aimed at enriching and supporting your experience. It is unique research practice involvement between the Accademia, museums, libraries, archives, industry initiatives and exhibitions. Together they create a rich tapestry of knowledge gathering, inspiration and in-depth research.

Individuals who have a passion for fashion whether they are artists, designers or researchers are welcome although with no background in fashion design. The goal is to embrace diversity in applications and reach out to artists, digital artists, designers and communicators interested in understanding the Italian Fashion System and Supply Chain.

Join an unique opportunity that combines peer learning with an experience during Fashion residency in Milan!

  • The applicant/s must be citizen from V4 country.
  • The applicants must be at least 18 years old.
  • Good knowledge of English language both spoken and written is required (Italian language is an advantage).
  • The main criteria for selection of the Fashion Residents include a professional approach towards creative work documented by previous work/projects and residency plans presented by the applicants in the application form.
  • The residency period is 2 months and lasts from June 1st to July 31st.
  • The amount of support for each artist is 6,000 EUR and is intended to cover living expenses, including accommodation, meals, transportation, and other routine expenses associated with the residency program recipient's stay.

This residency program is incomparable as it doesn't follow the format of a degree program. Instead, it offers a learning experience focused on research. When applying it's essential to present a defined research proposal that showcases your ideas from your own perspective. The ACM will actively support research endeavors providing residents with feedback before their final presentation.

Technical problems with online application and other questions should be addressed to Project Manager Martin Marciňa.

How to apply?

The application form must be submitted via My Visegrad by October 15 at 12.00 PM (noon).

The online application system opens at noon on September 15.

Your application must include the following enclosures:

  • Copy of your ID or passport
  • Your CV and motivation letter (including your project plan)
  • Artistic portfolio (file or link to artist´s website)

Applicants are selected on the basis of their previous work documented in personal portfolio, structured curriculum vitae (CV), motivation letter and a project plan.

Explore more

item.title: Performing Artist Residency UPCOMING Opens: September 15, 2026
item.description:
Performing Artist Residencies support contemporary theater and dance in Central Europe by providing opportunities to host artists and companies from/in V4 countries.

At-a-Glance Criteria

  • Eligibility & Scope: Applicants V4 citizens aged 18+, both individual artists and groups, may apply. The residency must take place in a V4 country other than the applicant’s country of citizenship/residence.
  • Artistic Focus & Timing: Supporting experimental and innovative performing arts and excludes stone theaters, finished productions, and festivals.
  • Funding: Residencies last 1 month; individual residency: €2,500 for the artist + €2,000 for the host institution. Group residency: €5,500 for group members + €3,500 for the host institution.

Guidelines & Files

Timeline

Sep 15, 2026 at 12:00 PM: Call opens

Oct 15, 2026 at 12:00 PM: Final application deadline

Dec 20, 2026 at 12:00 PM: Results announced

Jan 10, 2027 at 12:00 PM: Project start

Performing Artist residencies support innovation, experiment and creativity in the performing arts – new drama, contemporary dance, new circus, physical theatre, visual theater, alternative theater, performance art. The program is not suitable for stone theaters, already developed performances, or theater festivals.

  • Both individual artists and artistic groups can apply for this type of support
  • The applicant/s must be citizen from V4 country over the age of 18
  • Applicants for group residencies (3 artists or more) may come from different V4 countries (group members, however, must come from V4 countries other than the destination country)
  • The place of residency must be different than the applicant’s citizenship and residence
  • Each applicant can get support only once per calendar year
  • The length of support is 1 month
  • Residencies can take place between January 10 to December 31
  • The support for individual residency is €2,000 for the host institution and €2,500  for the artist
  • The amount of support for group residency is €3,500 for the host institution and €5,500 for the group members

For more information about general conditions and selection criteria, read Rules of the Visegrad Artist Residency Program.

The Final report is to be submitted by the artist and the host institution no later than 30 days after the end of the residency at the latest. The Final reports should be prepared with the help of the questionnaires.

To ensure the timely disbursement of the final installment, residents are kindly requested to complete the Questionnaire within 30 days after the conclusion of their residency. The questionnaire is completed through my.visegrad.org system.

Additionally, residents are required to upload images captured during their residency and provide web links to any related posts.

The host organization is responsible for completing, printing, and signing separate questionnaire. Following this, residents are kindly requested to upload completed questionnaire from the host organization (pdf file) as part of their Final Report through the my.visegrad.org system and submit the whole report. 

Technical problems with online application and other questions should be addressed to Project Manager Lenka Bučková.

The application form must be submitted via My Visegrad by October 15 at 12.00 PM (noon). The online application system opens on September 15 at noon.

Application must be submitted with the following documents:

  • Copy of your ID or passport (of each applicant if applying as a group)
  • Artistic portfolio includes reference and an active link to your performing video
  • Scan of letter of acceptance from the host organization in English on a letterhead paper no older than 3 months which includes the names of the artists; title of the project; planned dates of the residency; date; name and signature of the statutory representative

Explore more

item.title: Concert Quatuor Diotima 12 Sep 2026 / 19:00
item.description:
Event Slider

Date

  • 19:00 / Cancelled 19:00 / Sold out Saturday, 19:00

Location

Pricing

Ticket collection, subject to room capacity (max. 2 per person):

In-person – 2 hours before
Online – 2 days before (Cartão Gulbenkian Mais) and 1 day before (Cartão Gulbenkian), from 10:00.

  • Quatuor Diotima
  • Yunpeng Zhao Violin
  • Léo Marillier Violin
  • Franck Chevalier Viola
  • Alexis Descharmes Cello

Betsy Jolas

Béla Bartók

Maurice Ravel

György Kurtág

The Diotima Quartet is one of the most acclaimed string quartets of today, its name deriving both from the female character created by Hölderlin in the novel Hyperion and from a landmark string quartet piece by Luigi Nono. Its reputation for excellence has been built through close collaboration with Pierre Boulez and Helmut Lachenmann, as well as performances of works by Beethoven, Schubert, Ravel and Bartók. The Diotima joins the Kurtág / Jolas Cycle at Gulbenkian in a programme bringing together works by the two celebrated composers alongside pieces by Ravel and Bartók.

  • Quatuor Diotima
  • Yunpeng Zhao Violin
  • Léo Marillier Violin
  • Franck Chevalier Viola
  • Alexis Descharmes Cello

Betsy Jolas

Béla Bartók

Maurice Ravel

György Kurtág

The Diotima Quartet is one of the most acclaimed string quartets of today, its name deriving both from the female character created by Hölderlin in the novel Hyperion and from a landmark string quartet piece by Luigi Nono. Its reputation for excellence has been built through close collaboration with Pierre Boulez and Helmut Lachenmann, as well as performances of works by Beethoven, Schubert, Ravel and Bartók. The Diotima joins the Kurtág / Jolas Cycle at Gulbenkian in a programme bringing together works by the two celebrated composers alongside pieces by Ravel and Bartók.

item.title: Concert A Little Summer Suite 11 Sep 2026 / 19:00
item.description:
• Gulbenkian Orchestra

    In 1962, the Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation decided to establish a permanent orchestral ensemble. Originally with only twelve musicians (strings and continuo) it was named “Orquestra de Câmara Gulbenkian”. This collective was successively enlarged and today the “Orquestra Gulbenkian” (the name it has adopted since 1971) has a permanent body of sixty instrumentalists, a number that can be expanded depending on the repertoire.

    This structure allows the Gulbenkian Orchestra to interpret works from the Baroque and Classical periods, a significant part of 19th century orchestral literature and much of the music of the 20th century, including works belonging to the current repertoire of the traditional symphonic orchestras. In each season, the orchestra performs on a regular series of concerts at the Gulbenkian Grand Auditorium in Lisbon, where it has had the opportunity of working together with some of leading names of the world of music (conductors and soloists). It has also performed on numerous locations all over Portugal, in an effort to decentralize music and culture.

    The orchestra has been constantly expanding its activities in the international level, performing in Europe, Asia Africa, and the Americas. In the recording field, Orquestra Gulbenkian is associated to labels as Philips, Deutsche Grammophon, Hyperion, Teldec, Erato, Adès, Nimbus, Lyrinx, Naïve and Pentatone, among others, and this activity was recognized with several international prizes.

    Hannu Lintu is the Music Director of the Gulbenkian Orchestra since 2023.

item.title: Concert Kafka-Fragmente 09 Sep 2026 / 20:00
item.description:
• Marisol Montalvo

    Soprano

    The American soprano is among the most sought-after exponents of contemporary music working today. She is possessed of an extraordinarily flexible instrument, “brilliantly stratospheric” yet “sweet-voiced”, that has enabled her to achieve success in repertoire from Strauss to Boulez. A consummate, “unstinting” singing actress, she has been greatly acclaimed for identifying unconditionally with her characters.

    As well as performing alongside many of the world’s most renowned conductors and orchestras, she has had the privilege of working closely with many of today’s leading composers, including Matthias Pintscher, Olga Neuwirth, and Wolfgang Rihm. Several have written roles especially for her, including Peter Eötvos (Sierve Maria in Love and Other Demons), Pascal Dusapin (Prothoe in Penthesilea) and Marco Stroppa (Olbia in Il Re Orso). Her affinity for contemporary music has led to regular engagements with ensembles including Klangforum Wien, Ensemble Intercontemporain, International Contemporary Ensemble (ICE), Ensemble Remix and Ensemble Modern.

    Although she has achieved success in a wide range of operatic repertoire, Montalvo is particularly associated with the title role of Berg’s Lulu. Following her debut in the part at the Opéra National de Paris, Le Monde described her performance as a true revelation: “The American soprano possesses real stage and vocal presence, and executes the exhausting role with incredible intensity”. Subsequently, Lulu has become the centerpiece of her stage work; she has performed it at houses including Deutsche Oper Berlin, Théâtre du Capitole Toulouse, Teatro de la Maestranza, Theater an der Wien, Komische Oper Berlin, and at Theater Basel, in the acclaimed production by Calixto Bieto.

    Outside the opera house, Montalvo has a particularly close working relationship with Christoph Eschenbach, who has been both a mentor and a regular concert partner throughout her career. Since conducting her Carnegie Hall debut with the Philadelphia Orchestra, he has invited her to work with him alongside orchestras including the Vienna Philharmonic, the Houston Symphony, the London Philharmonic, the Munich Philharmonic and the Orchestre de Paris. Most recently, she performed the role of Sophie in a concert performance of Der Rosenkavalier with the National Symphony Orchestra under his baton at the Kennedy Center in Washington, DC.

    She has also worked with conductors including Daniel Harding, Vladimir Jurowski, Christopher Hogwood, Yuri Temirkanov, Bernhard Kontarsky, Sylvain Camberling, Sussana Mälkki, Lothar Zagrosek, and Sir Neville Marriner, and with orchestras including the Cleveland Orchestra, the Los Angeles Philharmonic, the San Francisco Symphony, St Petersburg Philharmonic, DSO Berlin, SWR Sinfonie-Orchestra, RSO Wien, Finnish Radio Symphony Orchestra, and the Bamberger Symphoniker. She has performed at houses including Opernhaus Zürich, Bregenzer Festspiele, Gran Teatro del Liceu, Baden-Baden Festspielhaus, Teatro Real de Madrid, Glyndebourne Festival Opera, Theatre du Chatelet, Théatre de Geneva, La Monnaie de Munt, Opera de Monte Carlo, Lithuania National Opera, Polish National Opera and Opera Comique.

item.title: Other Events Webinar Pioneering Renewable Energy Communities in Portugal 09 Sep 2026 / 17:30
item.description:
Event Slider

Date

  • 17:30 / Cancelled 17:30 / Sold out Wednesday, 17:30

Location

Pricing

This follow-up session to the webinar held on 21 July will showcase concrete experiences of creating and developing Renewable Energy Communities in Portugal, through the insights and experiences of some of the people involved.

Representatives of the Telheiras/Lumiar Renewable Energy Community, the Culatra Renewable Energy Community and Coopérnico will share the main challenges, lessons learned and impacts of these initiatives in a moderated conversation, followed by a Q&A session. The event will provide an opportunity to clarify questions and explore the potential of energy communities to foster citizen participation in the energy transition.

Launched by the Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation in partnership with Coopérnico, the Gulbenkian Energy Communities call supports civil society organisations seeking to develop community renewable energy projects in collaboration with local authorities or other local partners, promoting active citizen participation in the energy transition.

Selected projects may receive funding of up to €30,000.

The deadline for applications is 16 September 2026.

Partner entity

item.title: Grants Core Funding for Environmental Organisations Strengthening the capacity of organisations working to conserve nature and biodiversity. closes 07 Sep 2026 Open call
item.description:
In Portugal, more than half of all habitats are in decline. Civil society organisations working in nature conservation play a vital role in protecting biodiversity through the conservation, management and restoration of ecosystems. However, these organisations face significant funding and capacity challenges that limit the continuity and long-term impact of their work.

To help address these challenges, the Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation launched the first edition of this programme in 2025, awarding core funding to eight environmental organisations. The programme demonstrated the value of core funding in strengthening organisations’ stability, independence and capacity to deliver lasting impact.

With this second edition, the Foundation is renewing its commitment to supporting organisations that play an essential role in protecting the environment and safeguarding Portugal’s natural heritage. By complementing traditional project-based grants, core funding gives organisations the flexibility to strengthen their capacity and pursue their mission in a more sustainable and effective way.

Conditions

  • Financial support will only be awarded to legally established entities registered in Portugal;
  • The amount of each grant will be determined during the final selection process and will not exceed €50,000.

Eligibility

Applications are open to organisations officially recognised as environmental organisations under the National Register, or equivalent organisations, as well as organisations working in the field of nature conservation whose activities align with the objectives of this call and which meet the eligibility criteria set out in the Call Conditions.

How to Apply

  • Only applications submitted online will be accepted;
  • Register at  MyGulbenkian;
  • Before submitting your application form, check all the eligibility criteria and be sure to read the Call Conditions (available in the documents section);
  • Applications may only be submitted once all the mandatory fields of the form have been completed and the documents required under the Call Conditions have been uploaded;
  • Don’t forget to click “submit application”. Try not to submit your application in the last few days leading up to the deadline to avoid any unforeseen last minute problems.

Contacts

Questions about this call should be sent to: [email protected].

item.title: Concert Vale do Silêncio 05 Sep 2026 / 21:30
item.description:
• Gulbenkian Choir

    The Gulbenkian Choir was founded in 1964 by the Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation as a full symphonic body of around 100 singers. The choir joins the Orquestra Gulbenkian and other orchestras to perform Classical, Romantic and Contemporary choral-symphonic repertoire, but can also perform a cappella. It has performed – and often premiered – many 20th century works by Portuguese and international composers.

    The Gulbenkian Choir has been invited to collaborate with major international orchestras, under the direction of conductors such as Claudio Abbado, Colin Davis, John Nelson, Emmanuel Krivine, Esa-Pekka Salonen, Frans Brüggen, Franz Welser-Möst, Gerd Albrecht, Michael Gielen, Michael Tilson Thomas, Rafael Frübeck de Burgos, René Jacobs and Leonard Slatkin, among others.

    Besides its regular season of concerts in Lisbon and frequent national tours, the Gulbenkian Choir has repeatedly toured Argentina, Belgium, Brazil, Canada, Denmark, France, Germany, Hungary, India, Iraq, Israel, Italy, Japan, Macao, Malta, Monaco, Netherlands, Spain, the United Kingdom, the United States of America and Uruguay.

    The Gulbenkian Choir has recorded extensively for Philips, Deutsche Grammophon, Erato, Cascavelle, Musifrance, as well as FNAC-Music, performing a wide range of repertoire, from Early-Renaissance polyphony to Xenakis. Several of these albums received international awards.

    Martina Batič is the current Principal Conductor, succeeding Michel Corboz (1969–2019), Inês Tavares Lopes the Associate Conductor and Jorge Matta the artistic consultant.

  • Gulbenkian Orchestra

    In 1962, the Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation decided to establish a permanent orchestral ensemble. Originally with only twelve musicians (strings and continuo) it was named “Orquestra de Câmara Gulbenkian”. This collective was successively enlarged and today the “Orquestra Gulbenkian” (the name it has adopted since 1971) has a permanent body of sixty instrumentalists, a number that can be expanded depending on the repertoire.

    This structure allows the Gulbenkian Orchestra to interpret works from the Baroque and Classical periods, a significant part of 19th century orchestral literature and much of the music of the 20th century, including works belonging to the current repertoire of the traditional symphonic orchestras. In each season, the orchestra performs on a regular series of concerts at the Gulbenkian Grand Auditorium in Lisbon, where it has had the opportunity of working together with some of leading names of the world of music (conductors and soloists). It has also performed on numerous locations all over Portugal, in an effort to decentralize music and culture.

    The orchestra has been constantly expanding its activities in the international level, performing in Europe, Asia Africa, and the Americas. In the recording field, Orquestra Gulbenkian is associated to labels as Philips, Deutsche Grammophon, Hyperion, Teldec, Erato, Adès, Nimbus, Lyrinx, Naïve and Pentatone, among others, and this activity was recognized with several international prizes.

    Hannu Lintu is the Music Director of the Gulbenkian Orchestra since 2023.

  • Cláudia Semedo

    Apresentadora

    Cláudia Semedo é atriz e apresentadora de televisão. Nascida em Oeiras em 1983, completou o Curso de Interpretação da Escola Profissional de Teatro de Cascais em 2001 e licenciou-se em Jornalismo na Escola Superior de Comunicação Social em 2012.

    É presidente da Companhia de Atores e diretora artística do Teatro Municipal Amélia Rey Colaço, desde janeiro de 2017.

item.title: Meer lezen
item.description:
ELENITE/MAMAIA - Mutilated by political decisions that generate huge profits for certain companies, the Romanian and Bulgarian beaches on the Black Sea have become graveyards for tourists who are left at the mercy of natural phenomena exacerbated by the authorities.

Irresponsible decisions by the authorities in Romania and Bulgaria have led to natural and human disasters on the Black Sea beaches.

A flood of epic proportions swept across the beach at the Elenite resort in Bulgaria in 2025, claiming the lives of four people in a matter of minutes. A tragedy that could have been avoided had regulations regarding the protection of floodplains been adhered to.

But the local authorities allowed several tour operators not only to build hotels in the resort’s floodplain, but also to concrete over and narrow the natural channel through which the water could have drained away without affecting either the beach or people’s lives.

In Romania, a mammoth project to extend beaches along the entire coastline has created lethal hazards in the sea: particularly violent rip currents or, conversely, stagnant waters between breakwaters, with enormous pathogen potential, and beaches as hard as concrete.

The one-billion-euro project was carried through to completion against the advice of scientists.

Key Findings

Bulgaria

  • The tragedy on Elenite beach was caused by a series of administrative decisions over the last half-century.
  • The 1980 cadastral plan, for example, made no distinction between the region’s floodplain and the rest of the land.
  • After the 2000s, local authorities issued planning permission for hotels within the floodplain, and the buildings acted as temporary dams.
  • For practical tourism reasons, the floodplain was drastically narrowed and concreted over, causing floodwater to spill onto the beach.
  • None of these illegalities can even be attributed to anyone: the hotel owners who broke the law are hiding behind offshore companies in Cyprus and the Seychelles.

Romania

  • Right from the feasibility study stage, the beach extension project was flawed: the analyses and recommendations of scientists were ignored.
  • Instead of targeted beach extension solutions where erosion was most severe, the preference was for extension along the entire coastline.
  • The sand used was dredged from the seabed – this sand is coarse and contains a high proportion of shells, which has led to the destruction of the beaches.
  • The beach widening and the construction of new breakwaters have increased the number of rip currents, which are extremely dangerous for swimmers.
  • Several marine flora and fauna habitats have been totally or partially destroyed.

Methodology

The project methodology involved the use of legislative, commercial and geographical databases. As part of the project, Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) requests were submitted, and interviews and field visits were carried out to gather information.

Themes

  • Environment

Publication

ONLINE

  • Разливище: Заличената река в "Елените", която уби четирима, 24Chasa, 31/08/2026
  • EXCLUSIV Extinderea plajelor, un dezastru ecologic de un miliard de euro: curenți mortali, țărm distrus, faună și floră marine periclitate, Defapt, 27/08/2026

Countries

  • Bulgaria
  • Romania

Team members

Cătălin Prisacariu

Cătălin Prisacariu is an investigative journalist based in Bucharest, Romania.

Petru Zoltan

Petru Zoltan is a Romanian investigative journalist with nearly two decades of experience.

Stanimir Vaglenov

Stanimir Vaglenov is a Bulgarian journalist who works for Media Group Bulgaria. 

Related projects

  • © Pablo Fernández

    Who Owns Albania’s Coast?

    RRJOLL - From Rrjoll to Himarë, this investigation exposes how Albania's tourism model is driving the transformation of protected areas into luxury “resorts”, enabled by legal reforms and government decisions that favour private interests over environmental protection.

    Meer lezen
  • © under Creative Commons CC0 1.0 UNIVERSAL licence

    Under The Sun: The Hidden Trails of Solar Waste

    ROME / SOFIA / BUCHAREST – Proper recycling of PV panels can generate large quantities of raw materials crucial for the energy transition. Yet, due to the presence of harmful and toxic substances, solar waste can become extremely dangerous when it ends up in the wrong hands.

    Meer lezen
  • © Cosmin Filisan

    Climate Change and Mismanagement Deplete Water Reserves in Europe

    BARUTH / ORTONA / TÂRGU NEAMȚ - Across Europe, communities are facing a water crisis fueled by decades of poor groundwater management and climate change. This investigation examines the causes and consequences of water scarcity related to groundwater reserves in three of the most affected EU countries: Italy, Germany, and Romania.

    Meer lezen

Need resources for your own investigative story?

Journalismfund Europe's flexible grants programmes enable journalists to produce relevant public interest stories with a European mind-set from international, national, and regional perspectives.

Support independent cross-border investigative journalism

We rely on your support to continue the work that we do. Make a gift of any amount today.

item.title: Meer lezen
item.description:
ATYRAU - As the EU deepens its energy partnership with Kazakhstan, this investigation goes to the source of the oil that helps power European markets. Reporting from Atyrau, Kazakhstan's oil capital, it explores the social and environmental costs of decades of oil extraction.

In Atyrau, the air is often barely breathable. Residents and activists describe persistent coughing, burning eyes and growing fears over rising cancer rates. Since the arrival of Western oil companies in the 1990s, the city has been transformed from a quiet fishing town into Kazakhstan's oil capital, where almost every sector of the economy depends on the fossil fuel industry. While no direct causal link has been established between oil and gas pollution and cancer, incidence rates have been rising across Kazakhstan, with Atyrau consistently recording some of the country's highest figures. Through on-the-ground reporting, satellite analysis of oil spills, and independent water and soil sampling at sites that residents and activists have long identified as contaminated, this investigation examines the environmental and social costs of oil extraction, and the price local communities are paying for the energy that ultimately reaches European markets.

Methodology:

This investigation combined satellite imagery analysis, environmental sampling, and access to public records. We analysed data from the Transparent World dataset and Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 satellite imagery to identify oil spills in the Caspian Sea associated with operations of the Northern Caspian Operating Company (NCOC) consortium. In collaboration with local activists, we collected soil and water samples in areas adjacent to the city to verify the presence of contamination from petroleum products through independent laboratory analysis. We also submitted Freedom of Information requests to European Union institutions and the Italian authorities to obtain official documents concerning EU–Kazakhstan and Italy–Kazakhstan relations, with a particular focus on cooperation related to the country's energy sector.

Key Findings:

  • Laboratory analysis detected contamination from petroleum products, cadmium, chlorides, and sulphites in soil and water samples collected from two heavily affected areas of Atyrau, known as Kvadrat and Tukhlaya Balka. According to local residents and environmental activists, both sites have long been used for the illegal discharge of untreated wastewater generated by oil and gas activities.
  • Using Sentinel-2 satellite imagery, we identified four apparent oil spill events within the NCOC operational area in the Caspian Sea at different times during the past year. In response to our questions, the consortium stated that no oil spills have occurred within its area of operations since the beginning of its activities.

Themes

  • Environment

Publication

ONLINE

  • Kazakhstan, dove nasce il petrolio, Prismag, 02/09/2026

More to come

COUNTRIES

  • Italy
  • Kazakhstan

Nuri Fatolahzadeh is an independent Italian-Iranian reporter based in Lombardy.

Teresa Di Mauro

Teresa Di Mauro is an Italian independent journalist.

Benedetta Pagni is a science journalist and data analyst based in Trieste, Italy.

Aibarshyn Akhmetkali is a freelance journalist based in Astana, Kazakhstan.

Danil Usmanov is a documentary photographer from Kyrgyzstan.

Staffan Dahllöf is a freelance reporter based in Copenhagen, specialised in FOI.

    Inside the Global Trade that Moves PFAS Downstream

    VICENZA / LOTE PARSHURAM - What happens to a Western chemical plant after it closes down due to causing an environmental disaster? Sometimes it travels to other continents. This investigation reveals how a PFAS factory implicated in an Italian environmental scandal was dismantled and rebuilt in India, where production has resumed.

    Meer lezen

  • Dirty Money for Clean Rivers

    BUCHAREST - For almost 9 years, Romania has been criticised and monitored by the European Commission for allowing the large-scale destruction of several mountain rivers for the purpose of building micro-hydropower plants, without complying with the Water Framework and Habitats Directives.

    Meer lezen
  • © Modest Franco

    Shell’s Departure From the Niger Delta: Climate Action or Responsibility Dodging?

    BODO - This investigation, led by a team of journalists with diverse backgrounds, delves into Shell’s divestment strategy in the Niger Delta and its far-reaching effects on communities.

item.title: Meer lezen
item.description:
RUŽOMBEROK - As demand for paper packaging grows, pressure on Europe’s forests increases. An investigation into Mondi SCP in Slovakia reveals the source of its wood and raises questions about the transparency of logging practices and the future of protected forests.

The global production of paper packaging is surging, yet the rising demand for wood raises questions about sustainability. The Mondi SCP paper mill in Ružomberok is one of Europe's largest paper packaging producers. It uses around 2.2 million cubic metres of wood each year, but the origin of the raw material and the terms of its procurement are not transparent enough.

The investigation has revealed disadvantageous contracts involving state forests, inadequate oversight of logging operations and cases of wood from old-growth forests being used. Thanks to GPS locators, the team of journalists and activists from Slovakia and Germany have uncovered unsustainable logging in Slovakia's national parks.

Experts are warning that supplies of suitable pulpwood are dwindling, and that recycling cannot offset the impact of rising paper consumption. Unfortunately, the political situation in Slovakia is deteriorating. The Slovak government has recently approved a move that puts four national parks back under the control of the state forestry authority rather than conservationists, which makes unsustainable logging more likely.

Themes

  • Environment
  • Industry

Publication

ONLINE

  • Minister Taraba agrees new biomass boiler for Ružomberok paper mibognas, aktuality.sk, 17/01/2024
  • Pappe statt Plastik: Wie die EU-Verpackungswende die Nachfrage nach Holz antreibt, MDR, 30/08/2026
  • Sledovali sme, kde skončí drevo z národného parku. Pred bránou papierní sa GPS odmlčalo, aktuality.sk, 31/08/2026

Related projects

  • © Mélanie Wenger

    Timber Thugs

    BRUSSELS / ACCRA – The EU wanted to prevent further deforestation around the world with a new regulation on supply chains in the timber trade. But in Ghana it has the opposite effect.

    Meer lezen
  • © Davide Mancini

    Mozambique Plants More Eucalyptus to Feed Europe's Packaging Demand

    CHIMOIO / SANTARÉM – The EU countries consume more cellulose than they produce, and this growing demand is creating new business opportunities for some while resulting in the loss of land for others. This cross-border investigation examines the land grabbing in Mozambique fuelled by the European demand for eucalyptus pulp.

    Meer lezen
  • © Lenka Matoušková

    Green EU Subsidies in the Hands of Organised Crime

    PRAGUE - A cross-border team of journalists has focused on the potential corruption of solar energy support in the Czech Republic and Slovakia. More specifically, in the Czech Republic, the government has postponed changes to the law that would allow the state-guaranteed price of solar power to adjust to the decline in investment in solar power.

item.title: Scholarship at the Open Society Archives / Visegrad Fellowship Program (2) UPCOMING Opens: September 1, 2026
item.description:
Scholarships, Fellowships

Mobility (scholarship, fellowship), whether for study or research is a central part of our aim to foster creativity and promote understanding between people across borders. We look for individuals pursuing innovative ideas in science and education wishing to engage in conversation on development and cooperation in Visegrad region.

Visegrad Fellowship Program

The Visegrad Fellowship is a short-term stay for scholars and researchers in V4 countries other than their citizenship or residence.

Visegrad Scholarship Program

Visegrad scholarship supports Master’s and post-Master’s students and researchers for up to two semesters at institutions in Central and Eastern Europe.

Visegrad–Taiwan Scholarships

Visegrad–Taiwan Scholarship supports academic mobility for V4 doctoral and post-doctoral researchers to study or research in Taiwan.

Western Balkans–Visegrad Fellowships

The Western Balkans–Visegrad Fellowship is short-term individual stay for academics and researchers, supporting exchanges V4 → WB6 and WB6 → V4.

Research Grants at the Historical Archives of the EU

The Visegrad Fund and EUI offer grants for post-graduate scholars from CEE to research at the Historical Archives of the EU in Florence, Italy.

Scholarship at the Open Society Archives

A joint program with Blinken Open Society Archivum offers research fellowships at the Open Society Archives (OSA), CEU Budapest, Hungary.

item.title: Meer lezen
item.description:
BRUSSELS - It is everywhere, yet invisible. Hawala, an ancient, trust-based money transfer system, moves vast sums of cash around the world every day, leaving almost no trace. No banks. No paper trail. Just a handshake and a code.

Every year, billions of euros legally cross European borders in transparent transfers for private or professional purposes. But alongside these official channels, a parallel system operates in the shadows. Hawala is illegal in many parts of Europe, yet it continues to thrive as a sprawling, highly structured network linked to organised crime. It is used to launder the proceeds of drug trafficking, terrorism and human smuggling on a global scale.

An investigation into terrorism financing in Belgium led the authorities to one of the largest hawala cases ever uncovered in Europe. The inquiry is being led by federal magistrate Vincent Guerra, who was unequivocal: 'These are not amateurs. This is fully professional and beyond anything we could have imagined.'

Now, a team of European investigative journalists, working through the EBU Investigative Journalism Network (a cross-border collaboration of public broadcasters) is joining forces to map the full scope of the network, trace its links to international money-laundering operations, and reveal how legitimate businesses, sometimes unwittingly, have become part of the chain.

item.title: Grants Portugal + Preparado Supporting a project that contributes to developing a culture of earthquake preparedness and resilience in Portugal closes 31 Aug 2026 Open call
item.description:
Portugal faces a significant seismic risk, particularly in the Lisbon and Algarve regions. Although recent earthquakes have served as a reminder of this vulnerability, public and political responses have often remained intermittent and reactive, rather than part of a sustained, evidence-based approach to preparedness.

As part of its 70th anniversary celebrations, the Gulbenkian Foundation is launching this call to support the design and implementation of a project that brings together science, communication and public action. The initiative seeks to strengthen connections between academia, civil society and policymakers, helping to build a more informed and resilient society.

The project should contribute to improving public understanding of seismic risk, strengthening the preparedness of families, schools and organisations, and supporting more effective public policies and decision-making in the field of earthquake preparedness and resilience.

An online information session will be held on 18 June 2026 at 11:00 (Lisbon time). Enroll: [email protected]

Conditions

The maximum support available is €250,000, including taxes and any other associated costs. Projects may have a duration of up to 18 months. Proposals must not exceed 12 pages, excluding annexes.

Indicatively, proposals may address one or more of the following areas:

  • Knowledge and public policy – organisation of conferences, working groups and other initiatives that contribute to knowledge production and the development of strategic recommendations for policymakers.
  • Capacity building and awareness raising – development of educational resources, training activities, communication campaigns, earthquake drills and other initiatives aimed at schools, professionals, organisations and the general public.
  • Pilot and demonstration projects – implementation of experimental actions that test innovative approaches, generate practical evidence and support their future integration into programmes or public policies.

Eligibility

Proposals must be submitted by a single coordinating organisation with recognised scientific and technical expertise in the field of earthquakes and seismic risk.

The coordinating organisation may establish and lead a consortium with other relevant entities, while retaining overall responsibility for the strategic coherence, partnership coordination and delivery of the project.

How to Apply

  • Register to apply;
  • Before submitting the application form, check all the eligibility criteria. We advise you to read the Call Conditions (available in the Documents area, in Portuguese only)
  • Applications can only be submitted once all the mandatory fields of the form have been completed and the documentation required by the Call Conditions has been uploaded;
  • After filling the form, click on the ‘submit application’ button. In order to prevent difficulties in submitting applications, avoid submitting your application in the last few days of the deadline.
